Date: 2026-08-03T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: [Internal] Asterion sizing recommendations + runbook notes

Team — quick technical prescriptive notes after a first read of the traffic dump:

1) Workload shape
- Median request: 18 tokens output, average of 560 prompt tokens. Two burst days with ~3x baseline QPS for 6 hours.
- 95th token-length spike sits around 1024 tokens. Batch dynamics: many single-token streaming responses (low batching), some batched re-ranks during offline processing windows.

2) Target SLOs and safety headroom
- Customer p95 target: <=150ms for text-gen (streaming allowed). Recommend sizing for p95 <=120ms to allow fallback/latency envelope.
- Set warmup KV cache targets: pre-warm top 10% request prefixes; use prefix caching to shave 15–30% token latency on common flows.

3) Hardware & fleet suggestions
- Preferred node: 8xA10G per pool for steady throughput; add 2xA100 nodes for burst absorb (quantization-friendly models).
- Initial pool size: 24 8xA10G equivalence (estimate ~360 concurrent single-token streams at target latency) + 4 A100 slots for heavy long-sequence bursts.
- Headroom: allocate 25% additional GPU fraction for safety on burst days. We can re-evaluate after the first validation run.

4) Validation plan (what we will run in staging)
- Synthetic replay of load-profile.csv with actual token distribution and realistic client pacing.
- Two validation passes: cold-start (no cache) and warmed-run (with KV/prefix cache enabled). Measure p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
- Failure criteria: p95 > 150ms OR >0.5% error rate (model timeouts/oom).

5) Operational checks for cutover
- Canary routing rules (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30-minute observation windows.
- Auto-rollback triggers in Console tied to p95 and error spikes.

I'll attach a short sizing write-up and a runbook outline. Priya — assign owners for replay infra and test schedule.

Attachments: sizing-recommendation.pdf

-Karthik
